package_info.why_malicious: The xz package was compromised by an attacker who gained trusted maintainer access and inserted a sophisticated backdoor into the codebase. The malicious code was designed to subvert the SSH authentication process by injecting itself into liblzma, enabling remote code execution and unauthorized access on affected systems when a specially crafted SSH key exchange was performed.

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, when SSH authentication is performed via OpenSSH using the compromised liblzma library
execution_context.file_location: liblzma (xz/liblzma) source code, specifically in test files and build scripts (e.g., xz/tests/files, m4/build-to-host.m4, and liblzma/configure.ac) that are conditionally compiled and executed
required_permissions: filesystem (to modify or replace system libraries)
network (to enable remote command execution or communication)
process_injection (to hook into SSH authentication processes)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Obfuscated C code and shell script fragments embedded in the build system and liblzma source files. The code is conditionally compiled and, when built, injects a payload into the liblzma library. This payload hooks into the SSH authentication process, intercepts authentication requests, and enables remote code execution when triggered by a specially crafted SSH key exchange.
malicious_snippets.code_language: C (with embedded shell script components in the build system)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when SSH authentication is performed, the injected code hooks into the authentication process within liblzma, intercepts authentication data, and, upon receiving a specially crafted SSH key exchange, enables remote code execution or authentication bypass, resulting in unauthorized system access.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code is heavily obfuscated, conditionally compiled, and absent from legitimate upstream documentation. It introduces unauthorized hooks into the SSH authentication process via a compression library, which is highly anomalous and dangerous. The presence of undocumented payloads and manipulation of authentication logic in a non-authentication library is a strong indicator of malicious intent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Compression libraries like liblzma are expected to handle data compression and decompression only. They should never interact with authentication processes, modify SSH behavior, or enable remote code execution. The presence of authentication hooks and obfuscated payloads in liblzma is a clear violation of these expectations.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None. There are no legitimate scenarios where a compression library would contain authentication hooks or remote execution logic. Any such behavior is inherently suspicious and not found in normal software development practices.
key_indicators: Obfuscated and conditionally compiled code in liblzma and build scripts
Unauthorized hooks into SSH authentication processes from a compression library
Presence of undocumented payloads enabling remote code execution
Absence of legitimate documentation or changelog entries for the introduced code
Modification of test files and build scripts to trigger malicious compilation

attack_chain.action: Attacker gains trusted maintainer status and commit access to the xz project.
attack_chain.leads_to: Ability to insert malicious code into the xz codebase

attack_chain.action: Attacker inserts obfuscated, conditionally compiled malicious code into build scripts and liblzma source files.
attack_chain.leads_to: Backdoor payload is compiled into distributed xz binaries and libraries

attack_chain.action: When xz 5.6.0 or 5.6.1 is installed, the compromised liblzma library is present on the system.
attack_chain.leads_to: System is vulnerable to remote code execution via SSH authentication

attack_chain.action: Attacker sends a specially crafted SSH authentication request to a system using the compromised liblzma library.
attack_chain.leads_to: Backdoor is triggered, granting the attacker unauthorized access or enabling arbitrary code execution

behavioral_signatures: Obfuscated or conditionally compiled code present in liblzma or build scripts
Unexpected hooks or modifications to SSH authentication processes originating from compression libraries
Unexplained process injection or network activity initiated by liblzma or xz utilities
file_indicators: liblzma source files (e.g., xz/liblzma/common, xz/liblzma/check) containing undocumented or obfuscated code blocks
Build scripts (e.g., m4/build-to-host.m4, configure.ac) with conditional compilation logic not present in upstream versions
xz-5.6.0 and xz-5.6.1 tarballs with differences from verified upstream releases, especially in test files and build scripts
network_indicators: Unusual outbound connections or authentication bypass attempts from SSH processes linked against compromised liblzma
SSH authentication requests that succeed with invalid credentials or exhibit abnormal key exchange patterns
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Perform a file integrity comparison between installed xz/liblzma files and known-good upstream versions to identify undocumented or obfuscated code. Analyze build scripts and test files for conditional compilation logic or payload triggers. Monitor SSH processes for unexpected authentication behavior, process injection, or outbound network activity originating from liblzma or xz utilities. Flag any system where xz 5.6.0 or 5.6.1 is present and liblzma differs from upstream as potentially compromised.
